## Context

Make `src/rebar/_store/push.py` the authoritative CAS retry implementation before any workflow migrates. The current core stops after three merge attempts and discards the clean merge produced on its final iteration; the workflow carries five retries plus a final push. The core is also intentionally best-effort, while the reconciler's ephemeral commit-back requires an opt-in fail-loud disposition.

## Approach

- Extend `push_tickets_branch(base_path, *, strict=False)`; preserve the default for every existing caller.
- Use five merge/retry cycles and perform the final push after the fifth successful merge.
- Define one reusable `PushDeliveryError` carrying a distinct reason plus `N unpushed commits on <remote>/<branch>..HEAD`. Every strict CORE branch raises it; core never calls `sys.exit` or writes process streams.
- Cover terminal declines, rebase/merge-recovery guard, both store-epoch guards, final-push exhaustion, lock timeout, `sync.push=off`, `sync.push=async`, malformed destination config, and a missing configured remote.
- Preserve warning-and-return behavior byte-for-byte for the paired best-effort paths.
- Emit no ticket event and do not resurrect `BRIDGE_ALERT`.
- Keep `push_tickets_branch` push-only; dirty-tree staging/commit belongs to the dependent child. Add the dependency-first private adapter action `python -m rebar._store.push push --tracker ... [--strict]`; this is the sole boundary that catches `PushDeliveryError`, prints its message to stderr, and returns nonzero. Child 2bc9 extends the same adapter with `commit-and-push`.
- Update concurrency documentation to distinguish default best effort from opt-in strict delivery.

## Testing

Use real temporary git repositories for convergence and rejection, in-process fault injection at the actual guard/lock seams for the strict/best-effort branch matrix, and the existing real epoch fixtures for both epoch sites.

RED-first oracle:
- a deterministic competitor wins five pushes; current core exhausts three attempts and the expected remote/local convergence is RED;
- strict policy rejection must exit nonzero with the exact git reason, escalating unpushed count, and no new event file; current code returns;
- every strict branch has a paired best-effort control; core tests assert the catchable exception and a real module-CLI subprocess test separately asserts stderr/nonzero translation; semantic fault seams select branches, never source line numbers;
- large rejection stderr is classified by the Python core rather than YAML extraction;
- mutation removes the single final push and makes the contention oracle RED; a second-final-push mutation also fails the exact push-count oracle; warn-and-return mutation makes the strict matrix RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Five retry merges plus exactly one final push converge after five deterministic competing pushes; no duplicate final push is introduced and tests select semantic branches without navigating by source line number.
- [ ] Every strict core failure branch raises the reusable catchable `PushDeliveryError`; core never calls `sys.exit`, and paired core-boundary tests assert each distinct reason and unpushed count.
- [ ] The private module `push` action is the sole process boundary translating `PushDeliveryError` to nonzero plus stderr, proven by a real subprocess test; dependent child 2bc9 reuses and extends this adapter.
- [ ] Strict `off`, `async`, malformed destination, and missing remote configurations fail explicitly.
- [ ] Every paired best-effort case returns normally and preserves local commits and working-tree state.
- [ ] Strict failure writes no ticket event and never emits `BRIDGE_ALERT`.
- [ ] Direct `push_tickets_branch` remains push-only.
- [ ] Existing narrow-refspec, stash/pop, epoch-guard, and rejection-classification contracts remain green.
- [ ] Focused pytest nodes, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass.

## Compatibility and rollback

`strict` is keyword-only and defaults false, so existing CLI, MCP, library, importer, and store-write callers retain their contract. No persisted schema changes. This prerequisite lands unused and can be reverted safely before the dependent workflow cutover.
